classification.difficultyReason: The task links a binomial probability equation to algebra: recognise the squared product p(1-p), solve the resulting quadratic, and retain both valid probabilities.

content.prompt: When thrown, a push-pin can land either pin up or pin down. When the length of the pin is varied, the probability $p$ that the pin lands pin up will also vary. If a push pin is thrown four times, then the probability that it lands pin up twice is $\frac8{27}$. Find the value of $p$.

spec.sourceRegion: Beneath question 19 in the left column
spec.description: Two unlabelled push-pin orientations above one horizontal ground line: upright on the left and tilted with its point near the ground on the right. Decorative pale fill omitted.
spec.mathematics: Illustrates the two possible outcomes, pin up and pin down; no dimensions are specified.
spec.answerVisibility: Both orientations remain visible in the question.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ count pin-up outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}\Pr(X=2)&=\binom42p^2(1-p)^2\\6p^2(1-p)^2&=\frac8{27}\\\bigl[p(1-p)\bigr]^2&=\frac4{81}\\p(1-p)&=\frac29\\9p^2-9p+2&=0\\(3p-1)(3p-2)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $p=\frac13$ or $p=\frac23$. Both are valid probabilities.
